Re: Medical Necessity Appeal — Radiofrequency Ablation (RFA) / Medial Branch Neurotomy
CPT Code(s): {{cpt_codes}}
ICD-10 Code(s): {{icd_codes}}

Dear Medical Director / Utilization Review Committee,

I am writing to formally appeal the denial of prior authorization for radiofrequency ablation (RFA) / medial branch neurotomy for my patient. This procedure is medically necessary and is supported by the highest level of evidence from current multisociety guidelines and peer-reviewed literature.

CLINICAL SUMMARY

My patient presents with lumbar facetogenic pain confirmed by diagnostic medial branch blocks, requiring [urgency] intervention. Following comprehensive clinical evaluation using the RFA Compass™ clinical decision support tool (based on ASIPP 2013 and NASS guidelines), the recommended intervention is: [RFA Recommendation].

Region: Lumbar spine
Positive Diagnostic Blocks: 2 of 2 required



DIAGNOSTIC BLOCK REQUIREMENT MET

The ASIPP guidelines and the standard of care require two positive medial branch blocks (≥80% pain relief each) before RFA authorization. My patient has completed this diagnostic pathway, confirming facetogenic pain as the primary pain generator. The denial of RFA after confirmed diagnostic block response is not consistent with evidence-based guidelines.

GUIDELINE SUPPORT

This recommendation is based on the following evidence-based guidelines and peer-reviewed literature:

1. ASIPP Guidelines (Manchikanti L et al., Pain Physician 2013;16:S1–S111): Level I evidence for RFA in chronic lumbar and cervical facetogenic pain following two positive diagnostic medial branch blocks.

2. Spine (Dreyfuss P et al., 2000;25:1270–1277): 60% of patients achieved ≥90% pain relief at 12 months following lumbar RFA — superior to any other conservative intervention.

3. Randomized Controlled Trial (van Kleef M et al., Spine 1999;24:1937–1942): Significant pain reduction with RFA vs. sham at 3 months in appropriately selected patients.

4. NASS Coverage Policy: Lumbar medial branch neurotomy (RFA) supported for facetogenic pain confirmed by two positive diagnostic blocks, with pain duration ≥3 months and failure of conservative therapy.

MEDICAL NECESSITY

Without this intervention, my patient faces:
• Continued severe axial spine pain confirmed to be facetogenic in origin
• Repeated need for diagnostic/therapeutic injections without durable relief
• Inability to participate in physical therapy due to uncontrolled pain
• Significant functional impairment, reduced quality of life, and risk of opioid escalation

Conservative measures including physical therapy, NSAIDs, oral analgesics, and diagnostic injections have confirmed facetogenic pain but have not provided durable relief. RFA is the appropriate definitive treatment for this confirmed diagnosis.

REQUESTED ACTION

I respectfully request that you overturn the denial and authorize the requested radiofrequency ablation. I am available to discuss this case further and can provide procedure notes from the diagnostic blocks, imaging reports, and prior treatment records upon request.
